motions.item_title: Approve the minutes of the June 10, 2025, Planning Commission Meeting. Commissioner Whiting sec…
motions.motion: Commissioner Hess moved to approve the minutes of the June 10, 2025, Planning Commission Meeting. Commissioner Whiting seconded the motion.
motions.headline: June 10 minutes
motions.summary: The commission took up approval of the minutes from its June 10, 2025 meeting; the record does not show the result.
motions.impact: Minutes are the official record of the last meeting. You will not feel this one.

motions.item_title: Recommend approval to the City Council of Item 7.A. with recommendations that Project 19 connec…
motions.motion: Commissioner Whiting moved to recommend approval to the City Council of Item 7.A. with recommendations that Project 19 connect to Airport Road, Project 128 be removed completely, and that the comments from the Eagle Mountain Nature and Wildlife Alliance be included. Commissioner Strong seconded the motion.
motions.outcome: did not pass with a 2 to 2 vote and one abstained.
motions.headline: Changes to Projects 19 and 128 proposed
motions.summary: The commission weighed recommending Item 7.A with Project 19 connected to Airport Road, Project 128 removed, and the wildlife group's comments included.
motions.impact: This version did not go forward to the council in this form. Whatever Projects 19 and 128 are, this motion left them unchanged.

motions.item_title: Recommend approval to the City Council of Item 7.A. with recommendations that the comments from…
motions.motion: Commissioner Allen moved to recommend approval to the City Council of Item 7.A. with recommendations that the comments from the Eagle Mountain Nature and Wildlife Alliance be included. Commissioner Hess seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Item 7.A sent to council with wildlife group input
motions.summary: The commission recommended Item 7.A to the council, asking that comments from the Eagle Mountain Nature and Wildlife Alliance be included.
motions.impact: The record names the item only as 7.A, so its contents are not stated here. The council has the final vote and will see the wildlife group's comments alongside it.

motions.item_title: Table Item 7.B., Richard’s Animal Management Plan, until the July 8, 2025, meeting. Commissione…
motions.motion: Commissioner Allen moved to table Item 7.B., Richard’s Animal Management Plan, until the July 8, 2025, meeting. Commissioner Strong seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Richard's animal management plan delayed
motions.summary: The commission delayed a decision on Richard's animal management plan until its July 8, 2025 meeting.
motions.impact: This is one property owner's request. It waits two weeks, and neighbors have nothing new to react to yet.

motions.item_title: Table Item 7.C., A Proposed Amendment for Establishing Standards for Alternative Animal Managem…
motions.motion: Commissioner Allen moved to table Item 7.C., A Proposed Amendment for Establishing Standards for Alternative Animal Management Plans, until the July 8, 2025, meeting. Commissioner Fox seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Animal management plan standards put off
motions.summary: The commission pushed its review of proposed standards for alternative animal management plans to its July 8, 2025 meeting.
motions.impact: No decision was made, so the current rules still apply. Anyone following this item should watch the July 8 agenda.

motions.item_title: Recommend approval to the City Council of Item 7.D., Title 17 Amendments to Require Parking Lot…
motions.motion: Commissioner Allen moved to recommend approval to the City Council of Item 7.D., Title 17 Amendments to Require Parking Lots be in Proximity to Uses and to Standards Governing Shared Parking Arrangements, Commissioner Hess seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Parking lots must sit near the uses they serve
motions.summary: The commission recommended rules requiring parking lots to be close to the buildings they serve, plus standards for businesses that share parking.
motions.impact: Developers and business owners would design lots around these rules if the council adopts them. Shoppers might notice closer parking at future projects, but nothing is in force yet.

motions.item_title: Recommend approval to the City Council of Item 7.E., EMMC 17 Amendments to Drive-Thru Lanes. Co…
motions.motion: Commissioner Hess moved to recommend approval to the City Council of Item 7.E., EMMC 17 Amendments to Drive-Thru Lanes. Commissioner Whiting seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Drive-thru lane rule changes recommended
motions.summary: The commission sent the council a recommendation to amend the city code's rules for drive-thru lanes.
motions.impact: Restaurants and other businesses planning a drive-thru would follow the new rules once the council adopts them. For most people this one stays out of sight.

motions.item_title: Recommend approval to the City Council of Item 7.F., Table 17 Changes to Required Setbacks for…
motions.motion: Commissioner Strong moved to recommend approval to the City Council of Item 7.F., Table 17 Changes to Required Setbacks for Structures Housing Animals. Commissioner Hess seconded the motion.
motions.headline: New setbacks for buildings that house animals
motions.summary: The commission recommended that the council change how far buildings that house animals must sit from property lines.
motions.impact: If the council agrees, anyone building a barn, coop or similar structure would have to follow the new distances. The motion does not give the distances, and the council still has to vote.

motions.item_title: Recommend approval to the City Council of Item 7.G., Title 17 Amendments to Definitions and Con…
motions.motion: Commissioner Fox moved to recommend approval to the City Council of Item 7.G., Title 17 Amendments to Definitions and Controls Pertaining to Property Frontage. Commissioner Whiting seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Property frontage rules sent to council
motions.summary: The commission recommended that the City Council adopt changes to how the city's land-use code defines and controls property frontage.
motions.impact: Nothing changes yet, because the council makes the final call. The record does not say what the new frontage rules are, so it is unclear whose lots they would touch.
